newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - Jan 3.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - Jan 3.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
-- PENSION FUNDS HIT BY HIGH POUND AND CAUTION ON SALES

Figures from investment and pensions consultancy WM Company have revealed that the investment returns of UK pension funds fell sharply in 1996, to just 11.1 per cent compared to 19.1 per cent the previous year. The fall follows slower stock market growth, the strong pound, and caution among fund managers who fear a possible stock market crash.
-- THRIVING INDUSTRY IS HIRING MORE CONSULTANTS

An analysis by the Financial Times has revealed an explosion in the use of manufacturing consultants in Britain over the past three years. The study, involving 17 of Britain's largest manufacturing consultants, found that UK industry has spend an estimated 250 million stg on such consultants over the past year. The surge confirms the growing interest by multinational companies in expanding output from the UK.
-- MARKETS TAKE NEW YEAR FALL

Worldwide bond and equity markets have fallen sharply following American concern that the Federal Reserve may have to raise interest rates to hold back stronger US growth. The fall began in the US, where the Dow Jones Industrial Average lost 1.5 per cent on New Year's Eve. On Thursday, London's FT-SE 100 closed down 61.1 at 4,057.4. Stock market indices in Spain, France and Germany also closed down.
-- STERLING'S STRENGTH PUTS BRAKE ON FACTORY ORDERS

Figures from the Chartered Institute of Purchasing and Supply show that factory order books have weakened in the wake of the recent strength of the pound, contributing to a slowing of the expansion in the UK's manufacturing sector. The institute's purchasing managers' index showed a fall in December, the first such decline for six months. The figures indicate a cooling of the recovery in the sector, and may aid chancellor Kenneth Clarke as he resists calls to raise interest rates.
-- BRUSSELS PROBES BT/MCI LINK-UP

The proposed 12 billion stg merger of UK telecoms giant British Telecom and MCI of the US is to be investigated by the European Commission. The inquiry, which began on Thursday, had been promised by the Commission when the merger plans were announced in November. The Commission has one month to decide whether to clear the merger or whether to order a more detailed four-month inquiry.
-- POWERGEN DROPS INCINERATOR PLAN

Electricity generator PowerGen has announced it is to withdraw from a planned project to build a garbage incinerator on a site close to the river Thames in Kent, south east England. The project had been a partnership venture with waste management company Cory Environmental, but PowerGen has pulled out following a strategic review. The project had provoked environmental objections from local protestors.
-- LENDERS ATTACKED FOR OFFERING 'A POOR DEAL'

The Consumers Association, an independent body representing consumers' rights, has criticised large banks and building societies for offering poor deals to their customers. The Association's magazine Which? has advised consumers to avoid using the big banks and building societies for financial products, claiming they are too expensive.
-- REED ELSEVIER PLANS SCIENCE DATABASE

Publishing and information group Reed Elsevier has announced plans to establish the world's largest scientific database, offering all the group's 1,200 scientific journals on the system. Rival publishers of science journals will be invited to join the system, Science-Direct, on a commercial basis. Reed claims the database will contain twice the present volume of all the information on the Internet.
-- BANCO DI NAPOLI IN 4.7 BILLION STG DEBT CLEAN-UP

Italy's Treasury-controlled bank, Banco di Napoli, has transferred 4.75 billion stg-worth of bad debts and doubtful assets as part of the on-going privatisation process. The debts have been moved to a shell company to clean up the bank's balance sheet.
-- ATTACK ON ENVIROMED HOTS UP

US biomedical business Selfcare, which currently owns 29 per cent of the voting rights in diagnostics and healthcare group Enviromed, has succeeded in securing support from another large shareholder in its attempt to replace the board of Enviromed. Selfcare has called an extraordinary general meeting for later this month at which it hopes to complete the boardroom changes. BMC +44-171-377-1742
